stimulus.text: Researchers monitoring tide pools along a rocky coastline found that in pools where sea otters were regularly present, sea urchins were scarce. In pools from which sea otters were absent, sea urchins were abundant, and the seaweed that forms the base of the pool ecosystem was markedly sparse. Sea urchins are known to feed on seaweed. Taken together, these findings indicate that ______.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: sea urchins in tide pools feed on the seaweed that forms the base of the pool ecosystem
sea otters are the sole factor determining the abundance of sea urchins in tide pools
sea otters help sustain seaweed in these pools by keeping sea urchin populations low
sparse seaweed in some tide pools caused sea otters to abandon those pools

rationale: The inference requires combining the premises: otters present → urchins scarce; otters absent → urchins abundant and seaweed sparse; and urchins eat seaweed. The conclusion the premises jointly support is that otters, by suppressing urchins, help sustain the seaweed — a claim matched to the evidence in both scope and certainty (C). Choice A merely restates the premise that urchins eat seaweed rather than drawing a conclusion from all three premises together (restatement trap). Choice B inflates the supported claim into an absolute: the observations link otter presence to low urchin numbers, but nothing rules out other influences, so 'sole factor' overreaches. Choice D reverses the direction the premises establish: the pattern links otter absence to the subsequent abundance of urchins and sparse seaweed; it does not show seaweed scarcity driving otters away, and nothing in the passage addresses why otters leave a pool.
